consistent_scaling.evidence: THINKING STEP 1: Sessions and Pageviews both use counts (K) — unit match. THINKING STEP 2: Semantically related (web traffic metrics in same dashboard) — comparable. THINKING STEP 3: Dashboard intent 'Web Traffic' implies comparison. However required pixel-ratio check cannot be performed because there are no per-bar numeric value labels on the visible bars and the panels differ in axis scaling; the mandated pixel-ratio method requires readable numeric labels on 3–5 bars or unambiguous mapping from bar label-to-value. Unable to reliably measure true bar-top pixel heights tied to explicit numeric labels across panels, so consistent_scaling is unknown.

zoom_requirement.evidence: Charts include readable axis ticks and distinct bar/line differences; differences are visually discernible at shown scale and no inset/zoom is required for the typical comparisons shown.

labelling.evidence: Horizontal bar charts 'Device Sessions' and 'Channel Sessions' have no readable numeric y-axis ticks and do not include per-bar numeric labels, which violates the strict rule that per-bar numeric labels are required when no numeric axis is present.

violations.description: Horizontal bar charts 'Device Sessions' and 'Channel Sessions' lack a readable numeric axis and also lack per-bar numeric labels; when no y-axis ticks are present per-bar labels are required.

final_explanation: Overall the dashboard shows baseline zero on the main time-series panels (passes axis_baseline). Consistent-scaling cannot be verified because the pixel-ratio method cannot be applied without per-bar numeric labels. Labelling fails because horizontal bar charts lack both a numeric axis and per-bar labels, which is required by the rule.
